_what_this_is: The capability-coverage gate's ratchet. Every entry is a capability the strategy declares with NO requirement behind it, or a SCOPE commitment nothing downstream cites. Recorded 2026-08-12 at the product re-baseline. The gate fails on a NEW gap, and also fails when an entry here has since been covered but was left in place — a stale exemption is standing permission to regress.
_how_to_discharge: Write the requirement, then delete the entry. Never delete an entry to silence the gate; the gate will fail on the stale exemption, which is the point.
_last_discharge: 2026-08-13, re-baseline part 2 — nineteen requirement rows written. SEVEN entries paid in one fold: 13.3, 16.2 and all five SCOPE ids. The gate found every one of them itself, by refusing to pass with the stale exemptions still in the file.

_reasons._13_3_discharged: 13.3 Exception management DISCHARGED 2026-08-13 by REQ-DQR-004 — an owner, a state, an evidenced closure, and a re-open when the underlying rule still fails.
_reasons._20_3_discharged: 20.3 Performance attribution DISCHARGED 2026-08-12 by REQ-PRF-005. It was the gap the gate rediscovered unprompted on the day it was installed; it is the first entry paid.
_reasons._the_scope_class_discharged: All five SCOPE ids DISCHARGED 2026-08-13. Their shared defect WAS the mechanism of the Wave 1-17 drift: the strategy layer's own commitment vocabulary was spoken in exactly one file, so a commitment nothing downstream referenced could not be traced, could not be gated, and could not be noticed when it went unbuilt. They are discharged the only way that means anything — requirement rows that CITE the SCOPE id they serve: SCOPE-01 by REQ-INT-004 (input supplier, not filer), SCOPE-02 by REQ-PPM-009 and REQ-SMR-007 (a private sleeve and a public sleeve are the same kind of node; the admitted product-type set must cover both families), SCOPE-03 by REQ-MDG-004 (each of the six risk domains declared GOVERNED, PARTIAL or DECLINED, with counterparty DECLINED behind its triggers — an honest declaration rather than a claim of full coverage), SCOPE-04 by REQ-ADM-005 and REQ-DQR-004 (three lines, three refusals), SCOPE-05 by REQ-ADM-006 (one image, two deployment shapes).
_reasons._what_a_citation_does_NOT_mean: A cited SCOPE id means a requirement now answers to the commitment. It does NOT mean the commitment is built. SCOPE-02's derivative half remains the largest gap the re-baseline found — instrument terms carry seven bond fields and cannot express an option — and REQ-SMR-007 is precisely the row that will fail until that is fixed. Discharging a coverage gap makes the work visible to the process; it does not do the work.
